about: The Job page walks the plan in this order. Each stage lists step-id patterns in the order a technician works them; steps a stage does not name fall into 'other' at the end. Nothing here changes what runs, only the order and the words the technician sees.

stages.title: Check the device
stages.purpose: Make sure the device is online, not waiting on a restart, and (for dropship) is the unit that was ordered.

stages.title: Protect before changing anything
stages.purpose: A way back in if something goes wrong, the BitLocker key safe outside this device, and the user's files synced.

stages.title: Move the user to a local account
stages.purpose: Convert the Entra (Microsoft 365) sign-in into a local account JumpCloud can manage, keeping the user's profile and files.

stages.title: Disconnect from Microsoft
stages.purpose: Leave Entra ID and any AD domain, then clear leftover MDM enrollments, so JumpCloud is the only manager.

stages.title: Hand the device to JumpCloud
stages.purpose: Bind the user, put the device and user in their groups, and confirm JumpCloud policies apply.

stages.title: Security stack
stages.purpose: One EDR, the MDR agent, safe browsing, and Defender in the right mode.

stages.title: Updates, firmware and hardware
stages.purpose: The right update authority, Windows updates, OEM firmware, BitLocker back on after firmware work, and the hardware readiness report.

stages.title: Applications
stages.purpose: The client's standard apps, installed from trusted sources.

stages.title: Hardening, browser and branding
stages.purpose: The DE Windows baseline, browser policy, hostname and branding.

stages.title: Services, sign-off and handoff
stages.purpose: Backup, email security, MFA, remote support, site checks and the portal or people steps the plan needs.

stages.title: Deprovision
stages.purpose: Remove DE management safely, keep the client's data, and leave the client with an administrator.

why.net.connectivity: Installs and JumpCloud need the internet; nothing else is worth starting offline.
why.rescue.handoff: The boot rescue may have unlocked BitLocker with the recovery password, copied profiles or reverted updates; the next steps depend on what it did.
why.net.time: A clock that is minutes off makes HTTPS downloads, JumpCloud sign-in and the Hub signature fail with confusing errors.
why.maint.pending-reboot: Changing identity on top of a pending restart is how profiles get corrupted.
why.jumpcloud.agent: The agent comes first: its BitLocker policy is what escrows the recovery key in JumpCloud.
why.identity.breakglass: A hidden local administrator that always works, in case the migration or the Microsoft disconnect locks everyone else out.
why.identity.breakglass.verify: An untested break-glass password is not a way back in. Sign in with it once.
why.identity.bitlocker: The disk must be encrypted with a recovery password before identity changes.
why.identity.bitlocker-backup: Leaving Entra can take the only copy of the recovery key with it. A copy must be proven outside Entra first.
why.identity.onedrive: Files that have not synced yet are the ones a migration can lose.
why.identity.hello: The user's PIN stops working after migration; tell them before, not after.
why.identity.migrate: JumpCloud cannot take over a Microsoft 365 sign-in. ADMU converts it to a local account and keeps C:\Users\<user>.
why.identity.verify-migration: Proves the new local account owns the old profile before anything irreversible happens.
why.identity.hello-reset: Clears the old PIN container so the user can set a new PIN.
why.identity.entra-leave: JumpCloud should be the only manager. Leaving Entra and any AD domain comes after the migration is verified and the BitLocker key is safe.
why.identity.mdm-cleanup: Leftover enrollments from the old manager can fight JumpCloud policies.
why.jumpcloud.user-mapping: The local account, the JumpCloud user and the profile must all be the same person before binding.
why.jumpcloud.bind-user: Binding makes JumpCloud take over the local account and sync the user's JumpCloud password.
why.security.edr-conflicts: Two EDRs on one device fight each other and slow it down.
why.maint.update-authority: Exactly one system should control Windows updates (JumpCloud by default).
why.maint.warranty: An expired warranty turns a hardware fault into a purchase; the client should hear about it before the failure, not after.
why.maint.oem: Old BIOS and drivers cause the crashes and dock problems users call about. Dell uses Command | Update, Lenovo uses LSUClient (pinned), HP uses HP Image Assistant; BitLocker is suspended for one restart around firmware.
why.baseline.cis-audit: A read-only CIS or Microsoft baseline report shows what the DE baseline does not cover yet. It changes nothing on the device.
why.branding.lockscreen: The client's own lock screen on every PC: the company look before anyone signs in, the same image behind the sign-in box, no Windows Spotlight ads over it, and users cannot swap it for something else.
